accepted.match: "point" defined differently in elements-of-design and typography-basics
accepted.reason: Reviewed (0% overlap): genuine homonym. In Elements of Design a 'point' is the visual element — a mark of position/focus; in Typography Basics 'point' is the typographic unit of measure (1/72 inch). Different concepts that legitimately share a word.

accepted.match: "value" defined differently in elements-of-design and color-theory
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible treatments. Elements of Design introduces value as one visual element (lightness/darkness); Color Theory treats value as one of the three properties of color. Same underlying concept at complementary depths; non-contradictory.

accepted.match: "emphasis" defined differently in principles-of-design and visual-hierarchy
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible treatments at different depths. Principles of Design lists emphasis as one design principle; Visual Hierarchy applies emphasis as a means of establishing order of importance. Complementary, not contradictory.

accepted.match: "repetition" defined differently in principles-of-design and layout
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible treatments. Principles of Design defines repetition as a general principle; Layout uses repetition as the 'R' of the C.R.A.P. layout framework (Robin Williams). Same idea applied in two scopes.

accepted.match: "focal point" defined differently in visual-hierarchy and composition
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible treatments. Visual Hierarchy uses focal point as the primary attention target in an ordering system; Composition uses focal point as the dominant area of a single arranged image. Complementary framings of the same idea.

accepted.match: "format" defined differently in composition and grid-systems
accepted.reason: Reviewed (0% overlap): genuine homonym. In Composition 'format' is the shape/proportions of the picture frame; in Grid Systems 'format' is the overall page/canvas area the grid divides. Different referents sharing a word.

accepted.match: "legibility" defined differently in contrast and typography-basics
accepted.reason: Reviewed: compatible treatments. Contrast frames legibility as an outcome of adequate figure/ground difference; Typography Basics defines legibility as the distinguishability of individual characters, paired with readability. Complementary, non-contradictory.

accepted.match: "typeface" defined differently in typography-basics and typeface-classification
accepted.reason: Reviewed (8% overlap): compatible treatments. Typography Basics defines typeface via the font-vs-typeface distinction; Typeface Classification defines it operationally as the design family being categorized. Same concept, different emphasis.

accepted.match: the open textbook graphic design and print production
accepted.reason: Reviewed: shared run is the title of the openly-licensed BCcampus OER (Graphic Design and Print Production Fundamentals) that both topics cite by name. A source attribution, not duplicated exposition.

accepted.match: the rule of thirds and the golden ratio
accepted.reason: Reviewed: Principles of Design names the rule of thirds and the golden ratio in passing while surveying the principles and hands their depth to Composition, which owns them. The shared run is the canonical naming of two standard conventions, not duplicated teaching.

accepted.match: the web content accessibility guidelines wcag published by
accepted.reason: Reviewed: shared run is the standard attribution of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) to the W3C. Contrast names the standard and hands the ratios to Accessibility in Graphic Design, which owns them. Canonical attribution.
